This position is within the Protective Intelligence Operations Center (PIOC), Office of the Assistant Chief of Police for Protective and Intelligence Operations (ACOP-P&IO), in the United States Capitol Police (USCP).

The purpose of this position is to function as a PIOC Operations Manager/Executive Officer for the PIOC, exercising full programmatic responsibility for the management, direction, coordination, oversight, and continuous improvement of a 24-hour PIOC supporting Congressional protection missions, threat management, protective intelligence coordination, emergency communications, residential security monitoring, protective operations support, and continuity of operations activities.

Serves as the principal advisor to the PIOC Deputy Director on operational readiness, protective intelligence operations, program performance, strategic initiatives, policy development, resource allocation, contractor performance, and organizational effectiveness.

Ensures the effectiveness, efficiency, and mission readiness of all PIOC operations and serve as a key member of the Protective and Intelligence Operations (P&IO) leadership team. Provides overall management, direction, planning, and oversight of PIOC programs and operations.

Ensures the timely execution of mission requirements and the effective delivery of services supporting Congressional protective intelligence and protective operations missions.

Directs the day-to-day operations of the PIOC and establishes strategic and operational priorities for a 24-hour operational environment responsible for threat intake and triage, protective intelligence coordination, residential security monitoring, protective operations support, travel monitoring, emergency communications, and incident management.

Serves as senior advisor to executive leadership on matters affecting protective intelligence operations, emergency management, continuity of operations, and organizational readiness.

Conducts analyses of operational programs, policies, management processes, and organizational activities to identify issues, assess impacts, and develop recommendations supporting executive decision making.

Develops strategic recommendations regarding operational capabilities, resource allocation, staffing requirements, technology investments, and program modernization initiatives. Prepares and presents executive-level briefings, reports, correspondence, policy recommendations, legislative analyses, and operational assessments for senior leadership.

Serves as the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) or designated program official responsible for monitoring technical and administrative performance of contracted operational support personnel.

Provides executive oversight of threat management, intelligence intake and triage operations, event security coordination, law enforcement information sharing, residential security monitoring, travel monitoring, and protective operations support activities.

Oversees coordination among federal, state, and local partner agencies, as well as military, intelligence community, and Congressional stakeholders to ensure timely information sharing and effective operational support.

Provides executive oversight for significant incidents, emergency response activities, continuity of operations programs, and crisis management efforts affecting the agency’s protective mission.

Directs organizational response activities during critical incidents, emergencies, and major special events requiring executive-level coordination and decision-making.

Serves as a member of emergency response and continuity planning teams responsible for maintaining operational readiness during emergencies, natural disasters, civil disturbances, security incidents, and other disruptive events.
In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. For the CP-12 you must have at least 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to the CP-11/GS-13 level that is in or directly related to the line of work of the position to be filled.

Specialized experience consists of: 1) contributing to oversight and strategic direction for a 24-hour operational environment responsible for law enforcement or protective intelligence; 2) leading and directing complex research, intelligence analysis, and evaluation activities related to investigative operations to support operational strategy and organizational decision-making; 3) demonstrated experience formulating information source search strategies and evaluating data to identify patterns and relationships across criminal, public records or other sources; and 4) compile complex investigative information from a variety of sources in order to communicate and/or present investigative information orally and in writing to a variety of audiences.

All eligibility requirements must be met by the closing date of the vacancy announcement. (Information on Qualification & Education is located at the following link: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/)

Job Summary: In this role, you will provide technical leadership, coaching, and oversight to project ESH teams across a portfolio of manufacturing and technology projects. You will help strengthen ESH management systems, improve program consistency, support risk-based execution, and partner with project leadership to address significant concerns.

This role offers the opportunity to influence ESH performance at both the project and portfolio level while supporting high-impact work in fast-paced environments. #LI-AE2 Major Responsibilities: Shape strong project starts by providing ESH input to proposals, execution planning, risk assessments, resourcing strategies, and readiness activities.

Strengthen project ESH performance by coaching teams on ESH management plans, execution plans, permit-to-work systems, contractor management, and related specialty programs.

Drive consistent, high-quality ESH execution by overseeing program implementation and continuous improvement in alignment with applicable regulations and recognized management system requirements.

Improve program effectiveness by leading assessments, readiness reviews, audits, and conformance checks, and by helping teams close findings in a timely manner. Embed ESH into project delivery by partnering with engineering, construction, supply chain, subcontracts, commissioning, and project controls teams.

Advance portfolio learning and consistency by facilitating program kickoffs, risk workshops, constructability reviews, management system reviews, and knowledge-sharing forums. Support informed decision-making by preparing and reviewing ESH documentation, compliance reports, risk registers, objectives, and regulatory submittals.

Build alignment across stakeholders by working with project leadership, customers, regulators, auditors, and internal partners to address issues and coordinate support. Enhance visibility and execution performance by supporting ESH digitization initiatives and practical tools and systems.

Education and Experience Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety and Health, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, or a related field, with 14+ years of experience delivering ESH results in complex project environments.

Master's degree in a related field with 12+ years of experience advancing ESH performance in complex project settings. At least 5 years of experience supporting semiconductor, pharmaceutical/biotech, or hyperscale data center projects, with demonstrated impact on ESH performance.

Experience leading or advising ESH performance across multiple projects and influencing teams in a matrixed or functional environment. Strong knowledge of ESH regulations, industry standards, and management systems, including ISO 14001 and ISO 45001, with the ability to apply requirements in project execution.

Experience strengthening risk-based ESH programs through incident investigation, corrective action management, and continuous improvement. Ability to manage competing priorities, communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, and support teams in fast-paced project environments.

Familiarity with contractor management, compliance reviews, and contract requirements that support strong ESH outcomes. Valid driver's license required. Required Knowledge and Skills: Professional certification such as ASP, OHST, CSP, or CIH.

Working knowledge of OSHA, EPA, and key environmental regulations, with the ability to support practical compliance. Strong understanding of construction safety hazards, permit-to-work systems, JHAs, lockout/tagout, and critical control verification. Knowledge of industrial hygiene principles and chemical hazard management.

A day in the life: The AI Operations Manager is the operating system behind the Innovation team. You administer the company's enterprise AI platforms, keep the SVP and the team's initiatives moving in sync, keep the roadmap current, and act as an early-warning system for what is changing at the AI frontier.

Early on the work is operations-heavy; your strategic voice is expected to grow as you automate the operations down. You are a force multiplier, not a support function.

Responsibilities: - Administer the company's enterprise AI platforms - Claude Enterprise, ChatGPT Enterprise, Gemini, and new tools as we adopt them - covering provisioning, access, RBAC, usage governance, and billing, and automate that administration down over time. - Keep the SVP of Innovation organized and ahead of schedule through prioritization, prep, and follow-through - you catch what would otherwise slip before it does. - Run the Innovation team's weekly operating rhythm and keep the roadmap current and trusted at all times. - Produce a weekly AI intelligence brief on what is shipping at the frontier and what the team should test. - Bring a point of view into strategy conversations and grow into a genuine strategic voice for the team. - Utilize and leverage Power Digital's Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department. - Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements: 2-4 years of experience; early-career with an unusually high ceiling and a fast learning rate. AI-native - you use Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini daily and have real intuition for what they can and cannot do. This is the non-negotiable bar. A strong organizer who makes chaos legible and closes loops without being chased.

A clear writer and systems thinker who holds a point of view. Comfortable being the least experienced person in the room and still adding value. Meaningful daily overlap with U.S. Pacific hours (LATAM timezones ideal); remote, open to international candidates. Bonus: you have built something with AI - an agent, a workflow, or a shipped side project.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) - Enterprise AI platform access and provisioning requests resolved within one business day, fully documented. - Admin time trending down quarter over quarter as workflows get automated. - Weekly AI intelligence brief shipped on time, every week. - Roadmap accurate and current at any given moment - never a scramble to update it. - Zero missed commitments or dropped follow-ups traceable to coordination gaps.

Most Important Things (MITs) - Be the reason the Innovation team's operations run without friction. - Keep the SVP focused on the highest-leverage work by owning everything beneath it. - Turn AI platform administration into a system that mostly runs itself. - Act as an early-warning system for what is changing in AI - surface it before it is obvious. - Earn a real voice in strategy by being right, useful, and fast.

The Bureau of Human Resources proposes a structured, project-based student volunteer initiative within the Records and Information Management branch of the Office of Talent Services (HR/TS/RIM) at the U.S. Department of State.

This initiative directly supports the Presidential Management Agenda and Department priorities related to standardizing systems, eliminating data silos, and reducing wasteful processes.

Student volunteers will contribute to clearly defined, outcome-driven projects, including the documentation of standard procedures, conducting process mapping and proposing innovative modernizations, and updating SharePoint and ServiceNow systems with relevant information.

These efforts address a legitimate agency need to increase efficiencies as well as improve the usability, discoverability, and preservation of operational documents while supporting broader federal data and records management objectives.

The project is designed to align with student learning objectives by providing hands-on experience in process mapping and improvement, writing in Plain Language, lean management practices, and digital records management, while strengthening technical, analytical, and critical thinking skills.

Work will be scoped for completion within a single academic term and will include structured milestones such as onboarding and training, midpoint progress reviews, and final deliverables.

Deliverables may include process documentation, digitized Standard Operating Procedures cataloged in web-based systems, and research summaries that can be operationalized by HR/TS/RIM staff.

Goal: Improve the clarity, consistency, and efficiency of HR/TS/RIM's standard operating procedures (SOPs) by reviewing, revising, and standardizing up to 10 priority SOP documents using Lean management principles, Plain Language best practices, and staff input.

Objectives: 1) By the end of the Spring 2027 semester, review up to 10 existing SOPs; consult with relevant staff and partners to identify process inefficiencies, lessons learned, and opportunities for improvement; research and apply appropriate Lean management principles to develop revised SOP draft. 2) By the end of the Spring 2027 semester, create a culminating presentation to HR/TS/RIM staff and leadership about insights and lessons learned from SOP review, including any recommendations for additional improvements and practice adoptions for the office gleaned from interactions with staff and reviewing source materials.

Deliverables: By the conclusion of the internship, finalize and upload all approved SOPs to the designated digital platform using the organization's standard template, ensuring each document is written in Plain Language, reflects current practices, and is organized for ease of use and future maintenance.
Applicants will be considered based on their knowledge, skills or abilities related to project needs.

Specifically, applicants should possess: - Strong attention to detail - Research capabilities - Interest in management, process development, and digital records management Preferred qualifications: - Students pursuing degrees in business, public administration, communications, or related fields - Familiarity with process documentation and management practices - Familiarity with Microsoft 365 tools (e.g., Excel, SharePoint)

We are building a new proprietary crypto trading desk and need a Trade Operations Manager to run its day-to-day operations. This is a hands-on role. You will own the operational plumbing of the desk, ensuring every part of the trade lifecycle runs smoothly, accurately and at scale.
You'll sit close to the trading and engineering teams and report directly to the Head of Trading. Your job is to keep the trade lifecycle running with speed and precision, respond fast when something breaks, and turn a startup setup into operations that scale as our capital under management grows to multiple million euros.
This is ideal for someone who likes owning the details, wants real responsibility early and would rather fix the process than write a memo about it. It's an operator role, not a strategy or business-management role. If you want to run the machine day to day and see the impact of your work immediately, this is for you.
Tasks
What you would do
Trade Operations (your core)
Run the full trade lifecycle day to day: order execution monitoring, reconciliation, and reporting.
Own daily reconciliation across venues, custodians, and wallets. Keep it clean and keep it current.
Monitor execution in real time. Spot bad fills, routing problems, stale quotes, and slippage, and get them fixed fast.
Build and maintain the operational tools and workflows that keep trading activity running smoothly.
Incident Response & Reliability
Own the incident runbook. When something breaks (a trading error, a venue outage etc.) you are first responder and you drive it to resolution.
Track incidents, find root causes, and close the loop with the engineering team so the same thing doesn't happen twice.
Keep the desk resilient: monitoring, alerting, and clear escalation paths.
Process & Reporting
Improve operational processes continuously to cut errors, reduce manual work, and free traders from operational bottlenecks.
Produce clean operational reporting and KPI tracking for the Head of Trading.
Support coordination with exchanges, custodians, and other external operational partners.
Risk & Compliance (support)
Monitor risk exposures and trading limits day to day, and flag breaches immediately.
Operate the controls and reporting the desk relies on, and support the wider risk and compliance framework owned above you.

Experience in trading operations, trade support, middle/back office, or a related operational function in digital assets or traditional finance. A proprietary trading, hedge fund, or exchange background is a strong plus.
Hands-on mindset. You build and fix things yourself and you're comfortable in a lean, non-hierarchical setup without direct reports.
Sharp eye for detail under time pressure. Reconciliation breaks and execution anomalies don't slip past you.
Technical fluency: comfortable with Excel and SQL, and able to read or write basic scripts to automate operational work.
Calm and fast under incidents. You keep a clear head when something breaks in production.
Strong communication and organizational skills. You can run a process and keep the people around it informed.
Keen interest in blockchain, crypto, and DeFi is a definite plus.

Own the operational backbone of a trading desk being built from the ground up.
Work at the intersection of crypto infrastructure, systematic trading, and emerging financial markets.
Join a small, high-impact team where your work has an immediate and visible impact on how the desk runs.

Grove Collaborative is a sustainability-focused consumer products company creating household and personal care essentials that are effective, beautifully designed, and healthier for people and the planet. We are a certified B Corp, plastic-neutral, and on a mission to transform the CPG industry for good.
Merchandising Operations Manager
Grove's merchandising operation is full of good instincts running on manual work. This role exists to fix that: redesign the core processes, then personally build the automation that makes them stick. This is a rare shot at rebuilding how merchandising actually runs, and at proving AI belongs in the hands of the person closest to the problem, not just the AI team.
We're not hiring someone to write a strategy memo about AI and hand it off. We're hiring someone who will map the workflow, feel where it breaks, and then sit down and build the thing that fixes it.
More About the Opportunity
Merchandising at Grove runs on real expertise and too much manual glue.
Buyers chase vendors for the same data, week after week.
Marketing launches promotions inventory finds out about too late.
Good people spend their time on work a workflow should be doing for them.
We have an internal AI team. They coach. They don't build for you.
This role is for the person who wants their hands on the keyboard, not the person who scopes it and waits.
The honest version: no template here. You're defining the standard as you go, with review at key milestones and real autonomy in between.
Some of what you build will work on the first try. Some won't. That's the job.
What You'll Own
Map how merchandising actually works today, not how the org chart says it works.
Redesign core operating processes for speed, accuracy, and margin protection: assortment planning, item setup, pricing and markdown, vendor and PO management, allocation, replenishment.
Own the calendar connecting marketing activations to inventory, so launches are stock-backed, not a surprise to the warehouse.
Translate activation plans into buy, allocation, and replenishment signals; flag stock risk before launch, not after.
Coordinate vendor commitments tied to activations: fill rates, lead times, launch quantities.
Build self-service tools and proactive alerts that scale the buyer-vendor relationship, including visibility into vendor performance.
Build the automation yourself, using Claude and comparable AI tools, no/low-code platforms, and lightweight automation, from concept through rollout.
Run pilots end to end: scope, build, test for accuracy, validate fit, scale. Keep humans in the loop on margin- and inventory-critical decisions.
Maintain a registry of approved tools and active automations, so what exists and what it's for is never a mystery.
Own change management for every rollout: training, AI literacy for non-technical audiences, office hours, a bench of power users.
Build reporting on process and automation performance, and use it to prioritize what gets built next.

Real fluency in retail merchandising operations, not an adjacent function you've watched from a distance.
You've mapped a broken process and redesigned it, not just diagnosed it.
Basic technical acumen and a genuine willingness to build, no engineering background required.
Comfortable working with a specialist team as a coaching resource, not a build team, and taking their guidance without handing off your job.
You've run a pilot from scoping through adoption, and you know the gap between a demo and something people actually use.
You care about the boring, durable stuff: documentation, SOPs, registries, training, the things that outlast the person who built them.
You think in workflows and root causes, not tickets.
You know the difference between a problem worth automating and one worth leaving alone.
Even Better if You Have
Built something with Claude or a comparable AI tool that a non-technical team now relies on.
Experience connecting marketing or demand planning to inventory and allocation.
Designed a self-service tool that measurably cut manual buyer-vendor back-and-forth.
A retail, CPG, or commerce background with real fluency in vendor and marketplace dynamics.
